note.title: Pressure, density and fluids
note.overview: Pressure describes how concentrated a force is over an area. Density compares mass with volume. Together they help explain deep-water pressure, floating and many design choices.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: One pascal is one newton per square metre: 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
For the same force, smaller area gives larger pressure.
Pressure in a liquid increases with depth because more liquid is above.
Use compatible units: kg/m3 or g/cm3.
In a particle model, greater mass packed into the same volume means greater density.
An object tends to float if its average density is lower than the fluid and sink if higher.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: the SI unit of pressure, equal to N/m2
a liquid or gas that can flow
the space occupied by an object or substance
the upward force a fluid exerts on an immersed object
remain supported at a fluid surface when forces balance
move down through a fluid when weight exceeds supporting effects

quickCheck.question: Explain why a drawing pin has a sharp point and a broad head.
quickCheck.answer: The sharp point has small area, producing high pressure on the material.; The broad head spreads the finger force, producing lower pressure on the finger.
quickCheck.explanation: Key answer: The sharp point has small area, producing high pressure on the material.; The broad head spreads the finger force, producing lower pressure on the finger.

quickCheck.question: For Pressure, a student says: ‘Mass multiplied by temperature.’ Correct the statement and explain the science.
quickCheck.answer: State that the claim is incorrect.; Force acting per unit area.
quickCheck.explanation: Key answer: The claim is incorrect. Force acting per unit area.
